guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.title: Wedding Alcohol Calculator: Drinks Per Guest
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.desc: Work out how much wine, beer and spirits to buy for a wedding using drink-per-hour rules, guest mix and bar style, without over-ordering.
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.h1: How Much Alcohol for a Wedding
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.lead: The standard rule is one drink per guest per hour of the reception, then adjust for the mix of drinkers and whether the bar is hosted.
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.f1v: One drink per adult guest per hour of open bar
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.f2v: Count from the ceremony end, not the invitation time
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.f3v: A common starting mix is 50% wine, 30% beer, 20% spirits
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.f4v: Five glasses per 750 ml bottle; plan a case of 12
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.s1: Multiply adult guests by bar hours, then reduce for non-drinkers, designated drivers and children. A four-hour reception for 100 adults gives roughly 400 servings; at 50% wine that is 200 glasses or 40 bottles. Round up to cases, and buy from a retailer with a returns policy for unopened bottles.
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.s2: US receptions often run an open bar with a per-person package, so the calculator is a budgeting tool. UK weddings commonly include a welcome drink and wine with the meal but a cash bar later, which cuts the hosted volume roughly in half. In much of Europe wine is served with the meal by default and spirits consumption is lower; in some venues and cultures alcohol is not served at all.
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.s3: Two errors dominate: counting the whole day instead of bar hours, and forgetting that a champagne toast adds a separate serving for every adult. Also check the venue's corkage and licensing rules before buying anything — some forbid outside alcohol entirely, and a few require a licensed server.
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.q1: How many drinks per guest at a wedding?
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.a1: Plan about one per adult per hour of bar service, then adjust down for non-drinkers and up for a late-night crowd or a full open bar.
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.a2: For a four-hour reception with a 50% wine split, roughly 40 standard bottles, plus a separate toast pour if you are serving one.
guides.wedding-alcohol-calculator.a3: Many retailers allow returns on unopened, unchilled bottles with the receipt. Confirm before purchase and keep packaging intact.
